purpose: Per CEO R293: 'For every one of the existing 15, create: candidate → technical mechanism → problem solved → medical market → specific product category → top 10 potential buyers → buyer division → technical champion → economic buyer → current alternative → buyer pain → expected transaction range → evidence required → next experiment → TTP state → next commercial action. This becomes the Commercial Portfolio Master Register.'
constitutional_basis: Article X (canonical state). Article XXVIII (no silent promotion — each candidate has honest evidence state).

portfolio_restructuring.new_model: 15 diversified technology packages across 5 medical markets
portfolio_restructuring.rationale: Orthopedics: $60-68B market, 1000+ companies, asset-acquisition heavy (best for $50-500K packages). Cardiovascular: $62-79B, very active M&A (best for $500K+ packages). IVD: $128B, enormous buyer universe (best for software/algorithm packages). Surgical/enabling: large, fast-growing. Respiratory: large market, fewer buyers.

candidates.name: Rate-Limited Physiologic Conductance Control
candidates.technical_mechanism: Bounded-rate (2%/sec) conductance slew for multi-segment hydraulic drainage with sensor-health fallback
candidates.problem_solved: Shunt failure from obstruction (30-50% of shunts fail). Current shunts are reactive; P-01 predicts and redistributes flow proactively.
candidates.product_category: Active implantable shunt controller (Class III, PMA)
candidates.current_alternative: Codman Certas (reactive, manual adjustment), Miethke proGAV (passive gravity), VIEshunt (hardware but no rate-limited control)
candidates.buyer_pain: Shunt revision surgery costs $30-50K per revision. 30-50% of shunts fail from obstruction. No existing product predicts and prevents obstruction.
candidates.evidence_required: Physical bench validation of 2-3x computational advantage (80-run blinded protocol). FDA PCLC compliance pathway.
candidates.next_experiment: Build physical bench ($7-10K). Run 80-run blinded B-vs-V2.1 protocol.
candidates.evidence_engine: 35/47 executable (FDA metrics, ISO, VIEshunt, physiological, report generator)
candidates.next_commercial_action: Send Buyer Evaluation Kit to Miethke VP R&D. First technical evaluation conversation.

candidates.name: Conductance Governor
candidates.technical_mechanism: Adaptive valve pressure-response profile that adjusts drainage based on patient-specific compliance
candidates.problem_solved: Over-drainage and under-drainage due to fixed valve settings that don't adapt to individual patient physiology
candidates.current_alternative: Fixed-pressure programmable valves (Codman Hakim, Sophysa Polaris)
candidates.buyer_pain: Surgeons must guess the right pressure setting. Multiple adjustment surgeries. Patient outcomes vary with body position.
candidates.evidence_required: Computational model showing adaptive profiling outperforms fixed settings. Bench validation of pressure-response profile.
candidates.next_experiment: Build computational model of adaptive profiling vs fixed settings. Compare across 10 virtual patient profiles.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Define first falsification test. Identify buyer champion at Stryker or Globus Medical (spine division).

candidates.name: Residual Conductance Floor
candidates.technical_mechanism: Hard minimum drainage guarantee that prevents complete flow collapse under conservative controller behavior
candidates.problem_solved: Over-cautious controllers can reduce drainage too aggressively, causing CSF accumulation and ICP rise
candidates.medical_market: Neuro / CSF shunts (component of P-01 architecture)
candidates.product_category: Safety module for active shunt controllers
candidates.current_alternative: No existing safety floor mechanism in current shunts
candidates.buyer_pain: Fear of over-cautious control algorithms causing under-drainage in active shunt systems
candidates.evidence_required: Ablation evidence (already done: drainage floor is non-critical in most scenarios but HELPS in sensor_dropout). Physical demonstration of safety floor behavior.
candidates.next_experiment: Integrate into P-01 bench validation as a safety module. No standalone experiment needed.
candidates.evidence_engine: NOT STARTED — part of P-01 evidence engine
candidates.next_commercial_action: Position as P-01 safety module, not standalone product. Bundled with P-01.

candidates.name: Pulsation-Synchronized Catalytic Contact-Time Lock
candidates.technical_mechanism: Dynamically modulates CSF flow through enzymatic membrane synchronized with cardiac pulsation to maximize protein clearance
candidates.problem_solved: NPH patients with Alzheimer's comorbidity (>60%) need dual-function shunt: drainage + amyloid/tau clearance
candidates.current_alternative: Leqembi (IV anti-amyloid, $50-200K/patient/year). No existing CSF-integrated clearance.
candidates.buyer_pain: Leqembi is expensive, IV-administered, requires infusion center. No local CSF clearance option exists.
candidates.evidence_required: Phase 1 wet-lab: which enzyme survives 30 days in CSF? (3 months, $40-80K). Phase 2: immobilization. Phase 3: pulsation sync benefit.
candidates.next_experiment: Execute Phase 1 wet-lab program. Send collaborator package to 3-5 candidate labs.
candidates.ttp_state: PARTIAL (4/8 freeze items frozen, 4 blocked on biology. Phase 1 protocol complete.)
candidates.next_commercial_action: Engage enzyme engineering collaborator (MIT BME, Stanford BME, or CRO). Send COLLABORATOR_COMPLETE_PACKAGE.json.

candidates.name: Washout-Gated Drug Release
candidates.technical_mechanism: CSF flow-gated drug release module that delivers therapeutic agents proportional to drainage rate
candidates.problem_solved: Continuous drug delivery into CSF is difficult to control. Washout-gated release ties delivery to natural CSF dynamics.
candidates.current_alternative: Intrathecal pumps (Medtronic SynchroMed, Flowonix). Fixed-rate delivery, not flow-gated.
candidates.buyer_pain: Intrathecal pumps deliver at fixed rate regardless of CSF dynamics. Over/under-dosing is common. Battery replacement surgery every 5-7 years.
candidates.evidence_required: Computational model of flow-gated release kinetics. In vitro demonstration of flow-proportional release.
candidates.next_experiment: Build computational model of washout-gated release. Compare fixed-rate vs flow-gated delivery profiles.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Define first falsification test. Identify buyer champion at Medtronic Neuromodulation or Flowonix.

candidates.name: Selective Fail-Operational Membrane
candidates.technical_mechanism: Membrane that maintains filtration when partially occluded — fails operational, not fail-closed
candidates.problem_solved: Membrane-based filtration systems fail catastrophically when occluded. Fail-operational design maintains partial function.
candidates.current_alternative: Standard membranes that fail closed (no flow when occluded)
candidates.buyer_pain: Membrane failure in medical devices causes total system failure. No graceful degradation exists.
candidates.evidence_required: Computational model of fail-operational membrane geometry. In vitro demonstration of partial flow under occlusion.
candidates.next_experiment: Build computational model of fail-operational membrane. Compare flow curves: standard vs fail-operational under progressive occlusion.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Identify membrane engineering champion at Pall/Danaher or Sartorius. Define first test.

candidates.name: Drainage-Priority Clearance
candidates.technical_mechanism: Controlled release of therapeutic agents that prioritizes CSF drainage over clearance function (safety-first)
candidates.problem_solved: Dual-function shunts risk trading drainage safety for therapeutic clearance. This module guarantees drainage priority.
candidates.product_category: Safety controller for combination shunt products
candidates.current_alternative: No existing drainage-priority safety module for combination shunts
candidates.buyer_pain: Regulatory fear of combination products where therapeutic function compromises drainage safety
candidates.evidence_required: Demonstrate drainage is never compromised by clearance function. Safety analysis.
candidates.next_experiment: Computational model showing drainage floor holds even when clearance module is active.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Position as safety module for P-04. Bundled with P-04.

candidates.name: Energy-Neutral Micro-Assist
candidates.technical_mechanism: Energy harvesting from CSF flow/pressure to power implantable sensors without battery replacement
candidates.problem_solved: Implantable sensors need batteries that require replacement surgery every 5-10 years. Energy harvesting eliminates this.
candidates.product_category: Energy harvesting module for implantable devices
candidates.current_alternative: Primary cell batteries (Saft LM-175). Require replacement surgery.
candidates.buyer_pain: Battery replacement surgery costs $15-30K, every 5-10 years. Patient risk from repeated surgery.
candidates.evidence_required: Demonstrate sufficient energy harvesting from physiological flow/pressure. Power budget analysis.
candidates.next_experiment: Compute available energy from CSF flow (0.3 mL/min at 12 mmHg). Compare to sensor+controller power budget (1 mW).
candidates.next_commercial_action: Compute energy budget. If feasible, identify champion at Medtronic or Abbott implant engineering.

candidates.name: Chemical ICP Transduction Platform
candidates.technical_mechanism: Converts ICP into chemical molecular signal in CSF, detectable by wearable biosensor — zero electronics in brain
candidates.problem_solved: Current ICP monitors require batteries and electronics in the brain (infection risk, RF interference, replacement surgery)
candidates.current_alternative: Raumedic Neurovent (telemetric ICP, has battery), Codman MicroSensor (wired)
candidates.buyer_pain: All existing ICP monitors have electronics in brain. Infection risk. Battery replacement. No zero-electronics option exists.
candidates.evidence_required: Molecule-selection research program (6 steps, 14 months, $200-500K). 20-40% success probability.
candidates.next_experiment: Execute molecule-selection Step 1: candidate molecular mechanisms literature screen.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Engage medicinal chemistry consultant. Offer research collaboration or exclusive development option.

candidates.name: Phase-Change Valve Actuation
candidates.technical_mechanism: Valve actuated by phase-change material (solid-liquid transition) instead of electromechanical actuator
candidates.problem_solved: Electromechanical valves are complex, power-hungry, and have finite cycle life. Phase-change actuation is simpler and lower power.
candidates.current_alternative: Solenoid valves, MEMS valves, piezoelectric valves
candidates.buyer_pain: Electromechanical valves consume power, have cycle-life limits, and are complex to manufacture.
candidates.evidence_required: Material selection (phase-change temperature ~37°C). Power comparison vs solenoid. Cycle-life estimate.
candidates.next_experiment: Literature review of phase-change materials with transition near 37°C. Power analysis vs electromechanical.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Literature screen. Identify champion at Edwards or Medtronic valve engineering.

candidates.name: Phage-Based Anti-Biofilm Defense
candidates.technical_mechanism: Bacteriophage coating on implant surfaces that prevents biofilm formation without antibiotics
candidates.problem_solved: Implant infection from biofilm formation. Current solutions (antibiotic coatings) contribute to resistance.
candidates.current_alternative: Antibiotic-loaded bone cement, silver coatings, chlorhexidine coatings
candidates.buyer_pain: Implant infection rates 1-5%. Antibiotic coatings contribute to resistance. Biofilm is extremely difficult to treat once established.
candidates.evidence_required: In vitro demonstration of phage coating preventing biofilm. Stability data. Regulatory pathway assessment (phage = biologic?).
candidates.next_experiment: Literature review of phage-based anti-biofilm coatings. Identify 3 candidate phage species. In vitro design.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Literature screen. Identify champion at Stryker or Zimmer Biomet biomaterials division.

candidates.name: Enzymatic CSF Clearance
candidates.technical_mechanism: Enzyme-immobilized CSF clearance module that degrades pathological proteins (tau, alpha-synuclein) during drainage
candidates.problem_solved: Proteinopathies (Alzheimer's, Parkinson's) accumulate toxic proteins in CSF. No local clearance option exists.
candidates.current_alternative: IV antibody therapy (Leqembi, Kisunla). No local CSF clearance.
candidates.buyer_pain: IV antibody therapy is expensive, requires infusion center, has systemic side effects. No local option.
candidates.evidence_required: Enzyme selection (tau protease or alpha-synuclein protease). In vitro activity in CSF. Chronic stability.
candidates.next_experiment: Literature review of tau-degrading enzymes. Identify candidates. In vitro design.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Literature screen. Identify champion at Denali or Alector.

candidates.name: Neuromorphic Failure Predictor
candidates.technical_mechanism: AI-based implant failure prediction model using neuromorphic (event-driven) computing for ultra-low-power real-time prediction
candidates.problem_solved: Implant failure prediction requires continuous monitoring but battery power is limited. Neuromorphic computing enables ultra-low-power prediction.
candidates.technical_champion: Director of AI / Chief Data Scientist
candidates.current_alternative: Cloud-based ML prediction (requires data upload, latency, privacy concerns)
candidates.buyer_pain: Implantable devices can't run ML models locally due to power constraints. Cloud prediction has latency and privacy issues.
candidates.evidence_required: Demonstrate neuromorphic model achieves equivalent accuracy to cloud ML at <1mW power. Public dataset validation.
candidates.next_experiment: Train failure prediction model on public shunt/implant failure dataset. Compare accuracy: cloud ML vs neuromorphic. Measure power consumption.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Identify public implant failure dataset. Train baseline model. Approach Medtronic or Abbott AI division.

candidates.name: Production-Matched Drainage
candidates.technical_mechanism: Real-time CSF production estimation that matches drainage rate to actual production, maintaining zero net flow balance
candidates.problem_solved: Current shunts drain at fixed rate regardless of CSF production. Over/under-drainage occurs when production varies.
candidates.buyer_pain: CSF production varies diurnally and with hydration. Fixed drainage causes over/under-drainage.
candidates.evidence_required: CSF production estimation algorithm. Computational validation against physiological models.
candidates.next_experiment: Build CSF production estimator. Test against 10 virtual patient profiles with varying production rates.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Build production estimator. Approach Medtronic or Integra.

candidates.name: Self-Powered Physiologic Sensing
candidates.technical_mechanism: Self-powered implantable sensor that harvests energy from physiological motion (cardiac, respiratory) to power continuous sensing without battery
candidates.problem_solved: Implantable sensors need batteries. Self-powered sensing eliminates replacement surgery.
candidates.current_alternative: Battery-powered implantable sensors (Codman MicroSensor, Medtronic Reveal)
candidates.buyer_pain: Battery replacement surgery for implantable sensors. Patient risk. Cost.
candidates.evidence_required: Energy harvesting analysis from cardiac/respiratory motion. Power budget for sensing. Feasibility demonstration.
candidates.next_experiment: Compute available energy from cardiac pulsation (0.5-2 Hz, 10-30% amplitude). Compare to sensor power budget.
candidates.next_commercial_action: Energy budget analysis. Approach Medtronic or Abbott sensor engineering.

surgical_enabling.note: No current candidates map cleanly to surgical robotics. May reassign in future.

portfolio_optimizer_ranking.methodology: Rank = probability of buyer interest × technical evidence maturity × economic value × evidence cost (inverse) × time-to-buyer (inverse) × technology-transferability × potential transaction size

MEDIUM-HIGH — $75-250K potential, $0-5K validation (public dataset), fast to buyer (AI division)

MEDIUM-HIGH — $150-400K potential, $5-15K literature screen, ortho market is best for asset sales

MEDIUM — $150-400K potential, $5-20K literature screen, CNS biotech buyers

the_portfolio_optimizer_principle: If P-13 can reach a buyer with $5K of evidence while P-01 needs $100K of physical work, the machine temporarily prioritizes P-13. The portfolio optimizes cash generation + technical learning, not attachment to one favorite invention.
